target.title: feat: add durable routines registry
target.body:
Closes #98515

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw has cron jobs, tasks, heartbeat, commitments, and channel/session delivery primitives, but no first-class durable registry for recurring team-operations routines. Operators can schedule work today, but they cannot create, inspect, pause, delete, or recover a typed routine as one durable product object with ownership, delivery target, run status, and replay-safe mutation semantics.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds the smallest complete routine slice: a typed routine registry backed by the shared SQLite state DB, Gateway RPC methods, CLI entrypoints, and a schedule trigger that delegates execution to the canonical cron service rather than creating a second scheduler. The design keeps cron as the scheduler owner and routines as the durable registry owner, with internal create/toggle stages so retries recover safely after partial persistence or scheduler failures.

Non-goals for this draft: no Control UI yet, no channel-watch/repository-event/webhook triggers yet, no duplicate scheduler, and no transcript attachment. The trigger model is shaped so those future triggers can share the same routine subsystem instead of growing a second path.

AI-assisted implementation and review were used for this draft PR.

## User Impact

Users and operators can now use `openclaw routines` or Gateway RPC to create, list, inspect, enable, disable, and delete durable scheduled routines. Routine inspection shows owner, delivery target, enabled/deleted state, last and next run visibility, status, and last error context. Repeated create/toggle/delete calls are idempotent, and restart/replay behavior preserves the intended routine state instead of silently losing a schedule toggle or rolling scheduler state backward.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `7ede5834954ee58a4ac4afdf06a2615d8e2e92c3`, rebased on `origin/main` `44e88f550b699d6d3b6b236b557281f38d2ee8ab`.

- Protocol check passed after protocol/schema generation:
  `env PATH=/Users/steipete/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/node/bin:/Users/steipete/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/bin:$PATH /Users/steipete/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/bin/pnpm protocol:check`
- Testbox-through-Crabbox changed gate passed with provider `blacksmith-testbox`, id `tbx_01kwfpz4y5degwpa1swdzpr6rx`, Actions run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28546741204:
  `env PATH=/Users/steipete/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/Users/steipete/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/node/bin:/Users/steipete/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/bin:$PATH node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --provider blacksmith-testbox --blacksmith-org openclaw --blacksmith-workflow .github/workflows/ci-check-testbox.yml --blacksmith-job check --blacksmith-ref main --idle-timeout 90m --ttl 240m --timing-json -- env OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 corepack pnpm check:changed`
- Testbox-through-Crabbox build passed with provider `blacksmith-testbox`, id `tbx_01kwfpz63kx21neag8baewz1be`, Actions run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28546742243:
  `env PATH=/Users/steipete/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/Users/steipete/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/node/bin:/Users/steipete/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/bin:$PATH node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --provider blacksmith-testbox --blacksmith-org openclaw --blacksmith-workflow .github/workflows/ci-check-testbox.yml --blacksmith-job check --blacksmith-ref main --idle-timeout 90m --ttl 240m --timing-json -- corepack pnpm build`
- Real CLI/Gateway routine flow passed in an isolated Gateway setup with provider `blacksmith-testbox`, id `tbx_01kwfqj9mthmbczn7q6bkwec0p`, Actions run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28547315991. The proof built the branch, started `openclaw gateway run --dev --reset --allow-unconfigured` with a throwaway local token, then drove `openclaw routines create/list/get/disable/enable/delete` against that Gateway. Redacted output:
  ```text
  # build
  build: ok
  # gateway start
  gateway: ready
  # create
  { "created": true, "id": "proof-durable-routine", "enabled": true, "trigger": "schedule", "cronJobId": true, "status": "enabled", "delivery": "none" }
  # list
  { "count": 1, "ids": ["proof-durable-routine"], "enabled": [true] }
  # get
  { "id": "proof-durable-routine", "name": "Proof routine", "nextRunAtMs": "number", "cronJobId": true }
  # disable
  { "id": "proof-durable-routine", "enabled": false, "status": "disabled" }
  # enable
  { "id": "proof-durable-routine", "enabled": true, "status": "enabled" }
  # delete
  { "deleted": true }
  # list-after-delete
  { "count": 0, "ids": [] }
  ```
- Fresh autoreview against `origin/main` passed clean on exact head with model `koffing-updated`, extra-high reasoning. It explicitly reassessed best-fix fit, owner boundaries, LOC pressure, staged replay, scheduler ownership, delivery defaults, and split-vs-cohesive scope; result: no accepted/actionable findings.
- LOC gate after final rebase: production 21 files +2810/-310, tests 7 files +2321/-0, docs 8 files +342/-18, generated 4 files +325/-0. The branch remains a cohesive first-class routine slice; a split would separate recovery/schema/entrypoint pieces that need to be reviewed together.

Risks and review focus: routine persistence and cron mutation ordering, idempotent replay after partial failures, schema/client drift, schedule-only routine views over mutable cron backing jobs, and delivery target defaults. No UI screenshot evidence is included because this draft intentionally defers Control UI work.
